review_scope: In-process IPv4 static C11 library; not a network service

risks.title: Untrusted client IP identity
risks.scenario: The library accepts caller-supplied IPv4 identity; it cannot authenticate X-Forwarded-For or a peer address. A hostile caller can rotate or forge IP keys.
risks.mitigation: Integrating host must derive identity from an authenticated peer/trust boundary and normalize proxy headers before calling the library.

risks.title: Finite insert-only table
risks.scenario: A bounded table can be filled by distinct valid-sized IPv4 keys; after that new clients receive TABLE_FULL even when older clients are idle.
risks.mitigation: Size for traffic, monitor table-full decisions, apply front-door admission limits, and design eviction/reclamation separately if deployment requires it.

risks.title: Concurrent destruction is invalid
risks.scenario: Freeing index/bucket arrays while request workers are still accessing them can cause use-after-free.
risks.mitigation: Caller must stop ingress, join every worker, then destroy service; require lifecycle ownership in application design.

risks.title: Injected clock callback can block or malfunction
risks.scenario: The request service calls a user clock callback; its thread-safety, monotonicity and latency are external obligations.
risks.mitigation: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC or a tested thread-safe callback, avoid blocking inside clock code, and monitor CLOCK_ERROR.

risks.title: No network server or HTTP stack
risks.scenario: HTTP-style status decisions are in-process only; there is no socket listener, request parser, TLS, authentication, or wire response handling.
risks.mitigation: Embed library in a separately reviewed server, or do not market it as an HTTP reverse proxy or deployed gateway.

risks.title: Unstable public ABI
risks.scenario: Public structs expose C layouts; static library and headers must be rebuilt together on version changes.
risks.mitigation: Pin exact versions and rebuild/relink applications. Do not promise shared-library ABI stability.

risks.title: Packed-state limits and 64-bit atomic support
risks.scenario: Bucket packs 48-bit time and 16-bit tokens and initialization fails when required 64-bit atomics are not lock-free.
risks.mitigation: Validate policy ranges and lock-free capability at startup; use supported Linux/WSL toolchains and the compiled configuration.

risks.title: Operational counters are not a coherent live snapshot
risks.scenario: Five separately loaded relaxed atomic counters can describe different instants during concurrency.
risks.mitigation: For exact whole-system totals, quiesce workers first; otherwise treat snapshots as approximate telemetry.

risks.title: Benchmark gains depend on workload
risks.scenario: CAS synchronization can perform worse than mutex under some contention, CPU, and bucket layout combinations.
risks.mitigation: Measure p99, throughput and memory on target workload and hardware; keep the mutex baseline for comparison.

risks.title: CIDR rules immutable during traffic
risks.scenario: Mutating or freeing policy storage while workers use it is not a supported live reconfiguration mechanism.
risks.mitigation: Build rules before starting threads; stop/quiesce users for policy replacement or implement a separately verified snapshot strategy.

risks.title: IPv4-only identity and no eviction
risks.scenario: IPv6 identities are not supported; no expiry or cleanup of already-registered IPv4 identities is implemented.
risks.mitigation: Deploy only where IPv4 coverage suffices; document migration scope for IPv6 and reclamation.

risks.title: Tests are evidence, not formal global proof
risks.scenario: Sanitizer and bounded linearizability checks sample finite interleavings and cannot prove all concurrent executions safe.
risks.mitigation: Keep thread sanitizer and static analysis in CI and review CAS publication and lifetime assumptions manually.
